From: Lindsey Harper <l.harper@archwayhealth.com>

Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 16:24:00 +0000
Subject: Initial: VPC pricing question & on-call ops fee

Diego —

Thanks for the demo yesterday. Our procurement team is pulling together the commercial ask while engineering validates the footprint. A couple quick items that will drive the approval path on our side: 

- Can Redwood accommodate a staged commit (year 1: 30% commit, year 2: ramp to 70%) and amortize the platform fee across the staged commit?
- We need clarity on the on-call ops fee (monthly retainer vs hourly) and how that shows up on the invoice — our finance team wants predictable monthly amounts.
- Any standard implementation credit you offer for multi-cluster private installs?

I've attached a rough usage blend (Archway_Redwood_VPC_Usage_Blend.xlsx) for reference. Can you point to the guardrails and a worked example for invoice timing?

If useful, loop in pricing/legal — but ideally a clear term sheet and a short annex for SLA would get us to an LOI.

Thanks,
Lindsey Harper
Head of Procurement, Archway Health
(Attachment: Archway_Redwood_VPC_Usage_Blend.xlsx)

From: diego_fernandez@redwood.com
To: Lindsey Harper <l.harper@archwayhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 10:11:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Initial: VPC pricing question & on-call ops fee

Lindsey —

Appreciate the usage blend — that's very helpful. High level response and next steps below, then I will produce a short term sheet + SLA annex for signatures once we align.

1) Staged commit: yes. We can model a two-stage commit with an amortized platform fee. Typical approach is: spread the platform fee across the committed spend for the first 12 months for year-1, then re-amortize when the year-2 commit hits. That keeps monthly invoice predictability while preserving discount sequencing. I'll attach a worked example in the term sheet.

2) On-call ops: two options we offer:
   - Monthly retainer (recommended for production customers): fixed retainer covers N hours of on-call and a guaranteed SLA response window; any overages billed hourly. Predictable monthly line item.
   - Pay-as-you-go on-call: lower base, hourly invoicing for incidents (higher variance).

3) Implementation credit: we commonly provide a time-limited implementation credit tied to a committed node count and a 12-month ramp. For a rollout to 3 clusters we can offer an implementation credit applied as a contra invoice over the first 6 months.

Internal: Marissa — can we confirm the net discount ladder for a 30%->70% staged commit (3-cluster on-prem + 12-month retainer) and whether finance is comfortable amortizing the platform fee in the proposed way? Rishi, any guardrails on how we'll represent the credit on the invoice (contra vs one-time credit)?

I'll put a draft term sheet together (Redwood_VPC_Termsheet_v2.pdf) and SLA annex (Oncall_SLA_Annex.docx) for your review by Tuesday.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: Redwood_VPC_Termsheet_v2.pdf, Oncall_SLA_Annex.docx)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 14:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Re: Initial: VPC pricing question & on-call ops fee

Diego —

Thanks for the summary. Internals: we can approve the following commercial construct for Archway to keep the deal within our margin targets while being competitive: 

- Year 1 commit: 30% of targeted annual consumption, Year 2 commit: 70% (standard ramp). Discount ladder: 18% at year-1 commit level, 28% at year-2 full commit applied prospectively.
- Platform fee: $120k annual platform fee, amortized across the month-by-month invoices for year 1 (i.e., $10k/mo on invoices). If they hit the year-2 commit earlier, we re-amortize remaining platform fee across remaining months (subject to simple reconciliation).
- Implementation credit: $40k contra credit applied as credit note across the first 4 invoices (monthly offset) — this keeps AP workflow simple for the customer.
- On-call: recommend monthly retainer of $9k/month for 24x7 on-call with 1-hour P1 response SLAs; hourly overage at $250/hr.

Rishi — we should flag to finance that amortization will create a recurring invoice line (platform amortization) and a contra credit schedule for implementation. Let me know if there are tax/recognition concerns.

Marissa
VP, Commercial
Redwood Inference

From: Lindsey Harper <l.harper@archwayhealth.com>

Cc: procurement@archwayhealth.com
Date: Sun, 31 May 2026 09:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Re: Initial: VPC pricing question & on-call ops fee

Diego / Marissa —

Thanks, that reads well. A few clarifying items before we loop legal and finance for final sign-off: 

- Invoice timing: can you confirm invoices are monthly and that the amortized platform fee appears as a single line item labeled "Platform amortization"? We prefer predictable GL mapping.
- Implementation credit: applying as a contra note across first 4 invoices is fine, but can you confirm the credit note numbers will be visible on each invoice PDF?
- On-call retainer: 1-hour P1 response is acceptable. Can you add a calendar of escalation points (primary on-call -> engineering on-call -> director) to the SLA?

Once we have a short term sheet + SLA annex with explicit invoice samples, I can push this to legal/procurement and aim for an LOI the week of 6/7.

On a separate note: our CFO would like an option to pay the platform fee annually (prepay) at a 4% discount — would Redwood entertain that?

Appreciate the pace.

Lindsey
Head of Procurement, Archway Health
